title: PRD: Cohort-aware Hosted Endpoints — deterministic quality bands, tenant-aware burst, and staged rollback playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: High-level PRD for launching a cohort-aware hosted endpoint capability that enables deterministic quality bands per tenant, tenant-aware burst capacity controls, and a staged rollback playbook to reduce customer-impact during degradations.
objective: Deliver a hosted inference endpoint surface that: 1) enforces behavioral quality bands per cohort, 2) supports tenant-aware burst and throttling policies to protect shared pools, and 3) contains runbooked progressive rollback paths tied to telemetry signals.
scope_included: Behavior contract definitions and enforcement for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank
Per-tenant quality band configuration and default profiles
Tenant-aware burst rules and capacity hedging (Reserved vs. Shared lanes)
Canary + cohort progressive rollout tooling and guardrails
Operational playbook for detection, graded degradation, and rollback
scope_excluded: On-prem private deployment packaging (covered by Private team)
api_surface: Extend existing hosted /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints with optional query param 'cohort_profile'
Admin API to register cohort profiles: /v1/admin/cohorts (POST/GET/PATCH)
Telemetry tag 'cohort_id' emitted on requests and traces
Per-tenant override policy via tenant metadata (console + API)
api_examples: Client request: POST /v1/chat with body {model, messages, cohort_profile: "low_latency"}
Admin create cohort: POST /v1/admin/cohorts {id: "edu-light", quality_band: "band-b", burst_policy: {shared_burst: 2.0}}
performance_targets: P50 latency for 'low_latency' cohort: <= 70ms for token streaming start on hosted-dedicated nodes
P95 latency for default cohorts: <= 220ms for typical short prompts (<=128 tokens)
Throughput: sustain 1.5x baseline throughput for shared lanes with cohort-aware batching enabled
reliability_slos: Endpoint availability target: 99.95% across primary regions for cohorts in reserved lanes
Graceful degradation path: auto-fallback to lower quality band with <60s detection-to-fallback window
Canary health fences: fail canary if error rate increase >2% absolute vs baseline or latency regress >25%
security_requirements: Cohort registration API requires org-admin RBAC and audit logging to KMS-backed logs
All cohort metadata stored encrypted at rest, integrated with KMS
No cohort metadata or tags exposed in user-facing billing reports unless tenant opts in
acceptance_criteria: API: cohort_profile parameter accepted and honored for chat and generate endpoints (smoke tests pass)
Console: cohort creation UI flows exist with validation and a schema for quality_band and burst_policy
Behavior: for test cohort 'band-test-1' we can reproduce deterministic quality differences under synthetic load
Telemetry: cohort_id emitted on every request, traces can be filtered by cohort in Console tracing view
Rollback playbook: simulated degradation exercise executed with on-call runbook and postmortem template
Performance: verified P50/P95 targets met in 3 regions under representative traffic profiles
Security: cohort admin API access audited and encryption-at-rest verified in security review

rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Internal dogfood: enable cohorts for Redwood internal org only for 7 days
Phase 1 - Partner early access: invite 5 customers (mix of small-mid-enterprise) with manual monitoring for 14 days
Phase 2 - Gradual public opt-in: enable cohort param for all tenants behind FF (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated gating
Phase 3 - Default cohorts and console GA: expose recommended defaults in Console and remove hidden beta flags after 30 days of stable metrics
Canary rollback triggers: error rate delta, latency regressions, quality drift measured by eval harness, or security incident

metrics: Adoption: percent tenants using cohort_profile after 30 days
Quality delta: eval harness score delta between quality bands
Cost delta: tokens per request cost difference for cohort-aware routing
Incidents: number of degradation incidents attributed to cohort logic
Revenue ops: conversion rate for paid customers adopting reserved lanes
notes: Design decision: default cohort profiles will be opinionated to reduce configuration burden; advanced tuning behind 'advanced' Console panel
Trade-off: tighter per-tenant isolation increases orchestration complexity; start with soft limits and heuristics first
QA plan: synthetic determinism tests required to validate banding behavior; add deterministic seeds to rerank workloads
Operational nuance: burst policies should consider KV cache locality to avoid cold-start amplification
